clauses.reason: Section 1 establishes the Defense Meritorious Service Medal for award by the Secretary of Defense to members of the Armed Forces of the United States for outstanding non-combat meritorious achievement or service in joint assignments. EO 13666 (2014-04-18) amended it to extend eligibility to members of the armed forces of a friendly foreign nation; the clause continues, amended, with no end date, so it is operative on 2026-10-14.

research_rationale:
basis_pattern: original_plus_bounded_search. EO 12019 (signed 1977-11-03; 42 FR 57945; official Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12019.txt, read in full) establishes the Defense Meritorious Service Medal. Identity: heading, title and date agree with the register row. The dossier inventory omitted the authority recital and section 1 and covered only sections 2 to 4, so I replaced it with five clauses (inventory override). Own terms: no clause has an end date or ending condition. Later instruments: EO 13666 (signed 2014-04-18; 79 FR 22591, held Federal Register text) amends section 1 by inserting a phrase extending eligibility to members of the armed forces of a friendly foreign nation after the words naming members of the Armed Forces of the United States; by the strike-and-insert ruling of 2026-10-21 section 1 continues, amended. A search of held order texts for the number 12019 finds no other amending, revoking or superseding instrument, and the ofr_catalog search records only EO 13666. Current law: the U.S. Code (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; laws of 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 not reflected) prints EO 12019 as amended by EO 13666 as a note under 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, part II, chapter 57 (jobs/current-law/output/USC_EO_NOTES.jsonl and MENTIONS.csv). The order cites no statute as its authority (it rests on the Constitution and the President's office as Commander in Chief). The three selected machine searches were read with their coverage notes; none carries a coverage warning.
